claims.text: Use root user only to create an administrator IAM user with full permissions, then create other users/roles with limited permissions
Getting-started guidance: don't use root; create an administrator and use those credentials
IAM role used when identity isn't tied to a specific person: federated access, cross-account admin, AWS service access, EC2 apps (temporary credentials instead of stored access keys)
AWS Backup requires you to pass it a service role to assume for backup operations

A.notes: All supported; does not mention the instance profile mechanism for EC2.

claims.text: Don't use root user; create an administrator to manage resources
Use root only to create an administrator IAM user with full permissions
AWS Backup requires an IAM service role with permissions for creating, restoring, or expiring backups
An IAM role is chosen for an on-demand backup
An IAM role is assumed for the restore operation

B.notes: Does not answer when a role is used instead of a user; [3] text covers only the default role's create/restore permissions, not a requirement or expiring.
